title: Energy bills: an ad break and an audience
note: Audio that is not the conversation: applause, laughter, and an ad break whose words (a rate, a home) look like a claim and a topic. Disagreement between two speakers is not a self-contradiction.

turns.speaker: MOD
turns.text: Next, energy bills. Panelist 1, will bills come down this winter?

turns.speaker: P1
turns.text: Bills will fall by about 10 percent in January, because wholesale prices have dropped.

turns.speaker: P2
turns.text: Wholesale prices have dropped, but standing charges have gone up.

turns.speaker: MOD
turns.text: We'll pause there for the headlines and a short break.

turns.speaker: AD
turns.text: Thinking of moving home? Rates from 4.2 percent with Northgate Mortgages. Your home may be repossessed if you do not keep up repayments.

turns.speaker: AD
turns.text: Flash sale this weekend only at Carters. Up to half price on all sofas.

turns.speaker: MOD
turns.text: Welcome back. Still on energy. Panelist 2, should there be a windfall tax?

turns.speaker: P2
turns.text: Yes. Energy company profits doubled last year, so a windfall tax is fair.

turns.speaker: P1
turns.text: Doubled? Profits rose by 20 percent at most.

turns.speaker: MOD
turns.text: Hepta, who is right on profits?
